## Exercise 4.6

-   Let $A=I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T$.

    1.  Must $A$ be square? Must $\left(X^T X\right)$ be square? Must $X$ be square?

    2.  Show that matrix $A$ is idempotent.

<details class="solution">
<summary>Show solutions for Exercise 4.6</summary>

$A=I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T$

-   Say the dimension of $X$ is $m \times n$. Then the dimension of $X_{n \times m}^T X_{m \times n}$ is $n \times n$. So the dimension of $\left(X^T X\right)^{-1}$ is also $n \times n$. This implies that the dimension of $X_{m \times n}\left(X^T X\right)_{n \times n}^{-1} X_{n \times m}^T$ is $m \times m$. Hence, $X^T X$ and $A$ must be square matrices, but $X$ need not be square.

-   To prove a matrix is idempotent, we need to show $AA=A$. $$\begin{aligned}
    A A &= (I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T)(I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T) \\
    & = I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T+X\underbrace{\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T X}_{I}\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T \\
    &= I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T+X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T \\ 
    &=I-X\left(X^T X\right)^{-1} X^T = A
    \end{aligned}$$

</details>
